{"verdict": "correct", "claimsChecked": 44, "findings": [{"location": "Secs. 3-4, base stage j=1", "severity": "minor", "issue": "Several displays are undefined or false at j=1. These use T_{j-1}, V_{j-1}, C_{j-1}, A_{j-1}, H_{j-1} and the buffer-prefix bound S_old,11 >= N_{j-1}(A_{j-1}H_{j-1})^2. At j=1 there is no stage 0, the old rows are only e_1,e_2 (so S_old,11 = 1), and T_0 is not a support point. This does not affect validity: every statement is asymptotic in j, and finitely many n are irrelevant to convergence in probability.", "fix": "State the stage estimates for j >= 2, or treat {e_1,e_2} as stage 0 with T_0 := 0. Say explicitly that n up to the end of stage 1 is ignored."}, {"location": "Sec. 4, buffer prefix, last sentence (prefix coverage)", "severity": "minor", "issue": "The phrase 'the prefix immediately after completion of a previous stage' conflates two prefixes. The completed-stage prefix (k=C_{j-1}, ell=0) is covered by stage j-1's low-block argument. The prefix right after it is the buffer prefix treated in this paragraph. Coverage itself is complete: every n > 2 is exactly one of (a) the stage-j buffer, (b) a high prefix 1 <= h <= N_j, (c) a low prefix (k,ell) with 0 <= k < C_j and 0 <= ell <= 4, or (d) (C_j,0). The end of the high block is the low prefix (0,0), where both arguments apply.", "fix": "Replace the sentence with this explicit partition of n."}, {"location": "Sec. 4, low-block prefixes, u-equation, tightness and uniformity", "severity": "minor", "issue": "The argument is correct but uses informal o_P(1) bookkeeping. The exact u-equation is G_uu u + ell v + eta s_u = L_u, with G_uu = P_j + 8k + ell + S_old,11/A_j^2 >= P_j and |s_u| <= sum_old|a_i|/A_j + N_jH_j + 6k + 4. Also L_u/P_j = K_j + R_j + d_n. Here R_j is the lower-level high-block noise: it has variance V_{j-1}/P_j = O(N_j^{-27/10}) and does not depend on the prefix. The remainder satisfies |d_n| <= c_j -> 0 deterministically on the block tail events. The term written o(P_j) is actually o(1). The a priori system |u| <= X_j + 4|v|/P_j and |v| <= Y_n + 4|u|/(m B_j^2) has contraction factor 16/(m P_j B_j^2) -> 0. So the tightness step is not circular, and all bounds are uniform in (k,ell). This holds because the tail events are block-level and the (3.4) bound does not depend on the prefix.", "fix": "Display the exact u- and v-equations and name the prefix-independent error variables."}, {"location": "Sec. 5, (5.1)-(5.3)", "severity": "minor", "issue": "The claim v_tilde = O_P(1) is not needed at the completed prefix. There the cross Gram entry is exactly 0 and the u-sine term is deterministically O(N_jH_j + C_j), so u_tilde - (K_j+K'_j)/2 = o_P(1) follows directly. The final bound should name an explicit good set. Take E_j (probability -> e^{-2}/2), intersected with both streams' block tail events, |u_tilde - 1/2| <= 0.1, and (|L_tilde_v| + old sine)/C_j <= eta. On this set, g(0)/C_j >= eta(4cos(0.1pi) - 2sin(0.2pi)) - eta > eta. Since g' <= MQ <= 9MC_j, this gives v_tilde <= -eta/(9M). The liminf bound then follows from P(E_j) - P(rest fails), where the second term -> 0. This matches what the text asserts.", "fix": "State the explicit set and constants, and drop or mark as unused the O_P(1) claim for v_tilde."}, {"location": "Sec. 6 (Formal.lean)", "severity": "minor", "issue": "The Lean artifact was not reviewed; this verdict rests only on the written mathematics. Every component attributed to Lean was re-derived by hand: psi, the rho'' bounds 3/4..5/4, the profile score eta[4sin(pi u) - 2sin(2pi u)] (zero at integers, 4eta at 1/2), the weighted second-moment identity, and k/(b+k)^2 <= 1/(4b). Nothing in the proof depends on the artifact.", "fix": "None required for validity."}], "original_consistency_every_prefix": "established", "pooled_inconsistency": "established", "target_hypotheses_satisfied": true, "scope_statement": "This fairly refutes the TARGET formalization. Every stated hypothesis holds: p=2; one fixed nested deterministic design spanning from n_0=2; one fixed finite C-infinity rho with 3/4 <= rho'' <= 5/4 (hence convex and coercive); unique, measurable minimizers of both criteria for every n >= 2; an identifiable location-regression family (unique modal atom at 0, rows e_1,e_2); iid errors; and an independent same-law replicate on the same rows. Original weak consistency holds along all n and pooled weak consistency fails, so the universally quantified implication is false. This is consistent with Theorem 9, since here E eps^2 = E|eps| = infinity. It shows that the finite-variance hypothesis cannot simply be deleted, even for analytic, uniformly strongly convex rho. It does not refute the book. The book's unlisted 'certain conditions' would ordinarily include a well-defined population criterion, and this F violates every such condition: E rho(eps-t) = infinity for all t, and rho(eps-t) - rho(eps) = rho(t) - eps t on the support is not integrable for t != 0. It also says nothing about three further questions. First, intermediate hypotheses, such as a finite first moment only, or errors with a density (the exact reduction (2.1) needs lattice support in 2Z matching the period-2 ripple of rho). Second, strong-consistency versions: original a.s. consistency is not proved here, though the pooled failure would also defeat an a.s. conclusion. Third, non-pathological designs: rows reach 2N_j^11 with N_j = 2^(4*10^j). The correct reading is that the book's implication needs some condition on F beyond identifiability. Finite variance with strongly convex C^2 rho (Theorem 9) is one sufficient set.", "summary": "No fatal or major error found.

Reduction: (2.1) holds exactly for e in 2Z, because cos(pi e)=1 and sin(pi e)=0. All support points 0 and +-2N_j^2 are even. So both criteria reduce exactly to the deterministic D_n minus a random linear term, and the pooled criterion divided by 2 has the same D_n with the averaged score. Each cycle has Gram entries (8A_j^2, 0, 8), and an incomplete cycle has cross term at most 4A_j.

Scales: V_{j-1} ~ 4N_{j-1}^3 = O(N_j^{3/10}); sum_old|a| = O(N_j^{6/5}); sum_old|b| = O(N_j^{3/40}). The three block tail events have probabilities O(N_j^{-9/10}), O(N_j^{-9}) and O(N_j^{-1/4}), none depending on the prefix. The (3.3) exponents are -9/40 and -1/20. (3.4) gives the bound V_{j-1}/(4z^2B_j^2) = O(N_j^{-1/5}) uniformly, via (b-w)^2 >= 0.

Buffer and high prefixes: beta_1 = O(N_{j-1}^{-9}) and O(N_j^{-9}) respectively. beta_2 stays small because the buffer weight B_j^2 = N_j^{1/2} dominates the old cycles' sine imbalance O(N_j^{3/40}) while the new high block moves beta_1.

Low prefixes: u = K_j + o_P(1) uniformly, with K_j integer and tight, so the cycle profile score is at most eta*pi|u-K_j| per unit weak weight. The partial-cycle cross term is dominated by B_j^2, and the tightness step is a non-circular contraction.

Pooled at stage ends: u_tilde = (K_j+K'_j)/2 + o_P(1). The event K_j=1, K'_j=0 has probability -> e^{-2}/2. On it, the weak derivative at v=0 is about 4eta C_j with Q ~ 8C_j and curvature <= MQ. This gives v_tilde <= -eta/(9M) and liminf P(|beta_tilde| > eta/(20M)) >= e^{-2}/2.

Only truncated second moments, tail masses and symmetry are used; no infinite moment is invoked. All TARGET hypotheses hold. The remaining issues are presentational."}
